text_blocks.snippet: Illinois residents—including those in Central Illinois—are frequently targeted by active phone, text, and online scams.

list.snippet: Traffic & Toll Violation Text Scams: Scammers send fake text messages claiming you owe money for traffic tickets or toll violations, threatening to suspend your driver's license or vehicle registration if you do not pay immediately .
Imposter & Law Enforcement Scams: Callers impersonate federal agents, court officials, or local police (often using spoofed numbers) demanding fines for missed jury duty or active warrants.
AI Voice Cloning Scams: Criminals use artificial intelligence to mimic the voice of a family member claiming to be in an emergency or trouble, urging you to wire money or share financial data.

Fake DMV & Registration Websites: Unauthorized third-party websites (such as IllinoisCarReg.com) pose as official vehicle registration pages, overcharging users and harvesting personal data . Official renewals should only go through CyberDriveIllinois.com (or the Illinois Secretary of State's current portal).
Summer Travel & Vacation Scams: Phony vacation rentals, fake listings, and vague "luxury" travel packages target people planning getaways.
Door-to-Door Utility Scams: Individuals go door-to-door falsely claiming to represent energy suppliers (like Homefield Energy) to trick homeowners into changing or opting out of utility agreements.

Never click links in unexpected texts or emails: State agencies like the Illinois Secretary of State or Attorney General's office do not text or call to demand immediate payment, threaten license suspensions, or ask for Social Security numbers.
Verify the source independently: If you get a suspicious call or text, hang up and contact the agency or bank directly using the official phone number from their verified website.
Check official portals: Always manually type out official government URLs rather than trusting links in search ads or messages.
Report scams: File a report with the Illinois Attorney General's Consumer Fraud Bureau or the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) .
